title: openai-chat-completions-parity: streaming stability, functions/tool-calls, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting (v2)
author: Ethan Chen
description: Motivation: complete parity with OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics for roles, stop sequences, and logprobs while improving streaming stability and tool/function-calling compatibility. This PR addresses multiple customer-reported incompatibilities in the OpenAI compatibility layer: inconsistent role mapping for assistant/system/user, missing support for multiple stop sequences, incorrect or missing token-level logprobs in non-blocking streaming responses, and flaky streaming chunk boundaries that caused downstream SDKs to mis-parse function call payloads. Changes are grouped by area: API mapping (role normalization and backward-compatible aliases), streaming runtime (chunk coalescing, explicit flush markers, retry-safe resumable fragments), functions/tool-calls (structured function call tokenization and deterministic function call JSON reconstruction), response formatting (content/finish_reason/reporting of stop/logprobs), and tests. The description below documents scope, testing, and rollout: Scope: - Add comprehensive mapping layer from Redwood chat message shapes to OpenAI chat roles (accepts both 'assistant'/'system' and legacy 'bot' aliases). - Support multiple stop sequences and ensure they are honored deterministically across streaming/non-streaming paths. - Emit per-token logprobs and top_logprobs in streaming SSE chunks and in final aggregated response; ensure numeric precision matches existing API expectations. - Stabilize streaming by coalescing small tokens into stable chunks, inserting metadata frames for tool/function calls, and making streaming idempotent across retry windows. - Ensure structured output (JSON via function calls or structured_response hinting) rounds-trip correctly in both streaming and non-streaming flows. Testing & CI: - Add unit tests for role mapping and stop sequence edge cases. - Add E2E compatibility tests that run against the openai-compat harness used by SDK teams. - Add fuzz tests for streaming boundary conditions. Rollout & migration guidance: - Backwards compatible behavior: default mappings preserve current behavior when no explicit roles or stop sequences are provided. - Config flag 'openai_compat.explicit_roles' enables strict role validation; default false to avoid breaking existing customers. - Observability: added metrics openai_compat.streaming.chunk_size_distribution and openai_compat.functions.call_reconstruction_failures to help monitor rollout. Checklist: - [x] Role mapping implemented and unit tested. - [x] Multiple stop sequences honored and e2e tested. - [x] Streaming chunk stability fixes and SSE framing implemented. - [x] Function call reconstruction tested across SDKs. - [x] CI green after rerun. Related: ENG-1823 (role/stop parity), ENG-1841 (streaming stability), PM-402 (docs and SDK compatibility).

review_comments: Maya Patel: Please ensure the role aliasing table is documented; edge-case where 'bot' + 'system' both present should prefer explicit 'system' - Ethan replied: Updated docs and added unit test for conflicting roles to prefer explicit system.

Hannah Kim: Streaming coalescer looks good but is it safe for very long token outputs? - Ethan replied: Coalescer respects max_frame_bytes and will fall back to single-token frames when needed; added benchmark and metric to track chunk_size_distribution.

Carlos Vega: Are function call frames idempotent for client retries? We had a bug where partial frames caused double-invocations. - Ethan replied: Added explicit sequence metadata and server-side dedupe using request id + frame seq; added tests simulating retry windows.
Hannah Kim (follow-up): Integration tests initially failed in CI due to timing; reran and all checks passed.
ci_checks: integration: flaky on first run (streaming timing) then pass after rerun
benchmarks: show negligible regressed P95 latency for single-token streams, improved throughput for multi-request batching
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: improved role handling, support for multiple stop sequences, logprobs in streaming responses, and improved streaming stability.
Backwards-compatible by default; enable strict role validation via openai_compat.explicit_roles flag.
